subject: Political Science
textbooks: Politics in India since Independence, Class XII (NCERT)
Additional reference material (annexure to the CBSE document)
notes: Unit codes are prefixed A (Contemporary World Politics) and B (Politics in India since Independence).
Map questions can come from any lesson of Politics in India since Independence; cartoon and passage questions from either book.
Competency based questions will be 50% of the Class XII paper in 2026-27.

Additional reference material (not assessed): Arab Spring; BRICS; UNESCO, UNICEF and other agencies; terrorism; Patel and national integration; NITI Aayog; India-EU relations; Jaya Prakash Narayan; the Kashmir issue; NDA III, IV and V.

chapters.name: The End of Bipolarity
topics: The Soviet system
Gorbachev and the disintegration; causes and consequences
Shock therapy and its consequences
New entities: Russia, Balkan states, Central Asian states
India's relations with Russia and other post-communist countries
outcomes: Discuss the background and outcome of the Soviet disintegration
Assess the features of shock therapy
Trace India-Russia relations

chapters.name: Contemporary Centres of Power
topics: European Union
ASEAN
Rise of China as an economic power
Japan and South Korea as emerging powers
outcomes: Compare the EU and ASEAN
Evaluate China's rise and its impact
Summarise India's relations with China

chapters.name: Contemporary South Asia
topics: Military and democracy in Pakistan and Bangladesh
Monarchy and democracy in Nepal
Ethnic conflict and democracy in Sri Lanka
India-Pakistan conflicts; India and its neighbours
Peace and cooperation
outcomes: Appreciate the mixed record of democracy in South Asia
Justify the creation of SAARC
Understand the role of the US and China in South Asia

chapters.name: International Organisations
topics: Meaning and importance of international organisations; evolution of the UN
Principal organs of the UN
Reform of the UN after the Cold War; India and UN reforms
Key agencies: IMF, World Bank, WTO, ILO, IAEA; NGOs: Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch
Implications and future of international organisations
outcomes: Appreciate the role of the UN and its agencies
Understand the need for UN reform

chapters.name: Security in the Contemporary World
topics: Meaning and types of security
Traditional and non-traditional notions
New sources of threats
Cooperative security
India's security strategy
outcomes: Recognise the causes of security threats
Think critically about stakeholders in security

chapters.name: Environment and Natural Resources
topics: Environmental concerns; global commons
Common but differentiated responsibilities
India's stand on environmental issues
Environmental movements; resource geopolitics
Rights of indigenous peoples
outcomes: Explain global environmental issues
Appreciate India's responsibility in protecting the environment
Understand concerns of indigenous communities

chapters.name: Globalisation
topics: Concept; causes and consequences
India and globalisation
Resistance to globalisation, including in India

Evaluate its impact on India

chapters.name: Challenges of Nation Building

Integration of princely states: Hyderabad, Manipur
Reorganisation of states

Assess language as the basis of state reorganisation

Congress dominance in the first three general elections; Congress as a social and ideological coalition; factions
Emergence of opposition parties

First Five Year Plan; rapid industrialisation
